additional_requirements: The binge eating occurs, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

S051.name: Rapid_Eating
S051.description: Eating much more rapidly than normal.
examples: Swallowing food without chewing it properly.
Eating continuously and rapidly to the point where it is difficult to breathe.
Eating so urgently that there is no time to taste the food.
Eating at a speed that surprises others.

S052.name: Eating_Until_Uncomfortably_Full
examples: Eating until the stomach feels distended to the point of bursting and pain.
Eating so much that it is difficult to even stand up or move.
Continuing to eat until feeling nauseous or like vomiting.
Unable to stop eating even though it is physically uncomfortable and painful.

S053.name: Eating_Without_Hunger
S053.description: Eating large amounts of food when not feeling physically hungry.
examples: Starting to eat a large amount of food again immediately after finishing a meal.
A binge eating episode starting when not hungry at all.
Continuing to eat large amounts despite being full.
Seeking out food even when there are absolutely no physical hunger signals.

S054.name: Eating_Alone_Due_to_Embarrassment
S054.description: Eating alone because of feeling embarrassed by how much one is eating.
examples: Eating only when alone because of fear that others will think strangely of the amount eaten.
Eating secretly after family members have gone to sleep.
Pretending to eat little in front of people, then binging when alone.
Locking the door or eating in a secret place like a car to avoid being seen eating.

patient_info.stressor_event: Gaining a new family member (e.g., birth, adoption, older adult moving in)
patient_info.stressor: When Santiago’s older aunt moved into his El Paso apartment so she could be closer to family support, his home became fuller, warmer, and more food-centered, with extra batches of tamales, pozole, and tortillas always prepared for relatives stopping by. Across the following 10 months, he began staying up after everyone was asleep to finish large portions of leftovers alone, telling himself he was just avoiding waste, but finding that he could not reliably stop once he started and often ate rapidly until uncomfortably full even without hunger. He was embarrassed enough to keep these episodes separate from his usual sociable meals, especially because he was known as the generous cook who had things under control. He brought it up during a routine primary-care visit after a workplace wellness questionnaire asked about eating patterns, and he accepted a referral for psychiatric evaluation.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
S049.manifestation: On some nights after work, I can go through several tamales, a big bowl of pozole, tortillas, and whatever rice or beans are left, all while standing in the kitchen like I'm just cleaning up leftovers.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
S050.manifestation: What worries me is that once I start picking at the food late at night, I tell myself, 'That's enough, Santiago,' but my hand keeps going back like I don't get to make the decision anymore.

S051.name: Rapid_Eating
S051.description: Eating much more rapidly than normal.
S051.manifestation: I eat it fast, not like when I'm sitting with family, but more like I'm trying to get it done before anyone wakes up, barely tasting the food.

S052.name: Eating_Until_Uncomfortably_Full
S052.manifestation: By the time I finally stop, my stomach feels tight and heavy, and I have to sit on the edge of the couch for a while because bending over or lying down feels bad.

S053.name: Eating_Without_Hunger
S053.description: Eating large amounts of food when not feeling physically hungry.
S053.manifestation: A lot of times I'm not even hungry, because I already had dinner with everybody, but later I still end up opening the fridge and starting again.

S054.name: Eating_Alone_Due_to_Embarrassment
S054.description: Eating alone because of feeling embarrassed by how much one is eating.
S054.manifestation: I don't like anyone seeing how much I put away, so I wait until my aunt and the rest of the house are asleep and keep it quiet in the kitchen.

additional_requirement_1.name: Additional Requirement 1
additional_requirement_1.description: The binge eating occurs, on average, at least once a week for 3 months
additional_requirement_1.manifestation: For the past several months, it’s been happening most weeks at least once, usually on a night when there are plenty of leftovers and everyone else has gone to bed.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: I’m still getting to my shipping and receiving shifts and handling my responsibilities, but I’ve started avoiding some late family time in the kitchen because I’m worried someone will notice how uneasy I am around the food.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This has been going on for about 10 months, since my aunt moved into the apartment and there always seemed to be extra food around.
